lines.japanese: いやー、しまった。
lines.english: Well, I'd really done it this time.

lines.japanese: 眠い、眠いっす。皆さんも一度は経験がありますよね？
lines.english: God, I was tired. So tired. You've all done this at least once, right?

lines.japanese: 調子に乗って１ページ、もう１ページと進めていくうちに、時間がとんでもないことになっていて、そのまま仕事や授業に出ちゃったことって。
lines.english: You get carried away and turn one more page, then one more, and before you know it, it's some ungodly hour and you have to stumble straight into work or class.

lines.japanese: 睡眠不足は慣れっこなんですけどね……はは、限度ってもんがありました。
lines.english: I was used to getting too little sleep... Ha ha. Apparently even I had limits.

lines.japanese: いやぶっちゃけきついっす……今日はこのあとも米田さんにアポ取ってあるから、祥玄社さんにお邪魔する予定もあったんですよね。
lines.english: Honestly, this was murder... And after my shift I had an appointment with Yoneda, which meant stopping by Shogensha too.

lines.japanese: ま、でもようやく完成した細川玉木レビューを受けとってもらえるかと思うと、やる気だけは満点ってもんです。
lines.english: Still, with my finished Tamaki Hosokawa review finally ready to hand over, my enthusiasm was a perfect ten, if nothing else.

lines.japanese: ていうか、一日の行動のほとんどが日和子さんに関係してるってどうよ。
lines.english: Come to think of it, almost everything I did today had something to do with Hiyoko. What did that say about me?

lines.japanese: 我ながら偏愛。一歩間違えればストーカーっすな。
lines.english: Call it obsession. One wrong turn and I'd be a stalker.

lines.japanese: いやでも偏愛ついでに言わせてもらえれば、細川玉木の三作目。これすごい。
lines.english: But while I was confessing my obsession, let me say this about Tamaki Hosokawa's third novel: it was incredible.

lines.japanese: めでたく出版された暁には、また米田さんに売りこんでレビューを書きたいぐらいです。
lines.english: If it ever saw print, I'd happily pitch Yoneda on another review myself.

lines.japanese: 一作目『ほほえみインサイド』もデビュー作としての若さがつまっていて充分な佳作でしたが、今回は言うなれば意欲作！　も、自信を持ってお勧めしたいこの一冊！
lines.english: Her debut, *Smile Inside*, had been a fine piece of work, packed with all the youth of a first novel. This one, though—this was ambitious! A book I could recommend without reservation!

lines.japanese: 俺なんか読みふけっちゃって、あ、ふわ……。
lines.english: I got so absorbed in it that—ah, fwaaah...

lines.japanese: って、眠い、眠いいい……これは本格的にやばいかもしれない……誰か眠気をふっとばすぶっとびボルテージを与えてくれないかなあ。
lines.english: No, I was sleepy. So sleeeepy... This might actually be bad. Couldn't somebody hit me with a jolt of lunatic high voltage and blast the drowsiness clean away?

lines.japanese: 「おはよざーっす……」
lines.english: “Mornin'...”

lines.japanese: 「先日マンハッタンのバーへ行きました。右手にウイスキーグラス、胸元には赤い薔薇。左手はいつも空けています。何故かって？　それはもちろん、素敵なご婦人に出逢ったとき、すぐに握手ができるようにですよ」
lines.english: “The other day I visited a bar in Manhattan. A whiskey glass in my right hand, a red rose at my breast. My left hand I always keep free. Why, you ask? Why, so that when I meet a lovely lady, I may offer it to her at once.”

lines.japanese: ああ、よかった。眠気ふきとびましたよ、いろんな意味で。
lines.english: Ah, good. I was wide awake now, in every possible sense.

lines.japanese: はあ……マスターったら、相変わらず無駄に渋い声でしょーもない放送を……。
lines.english: Sigh... The boss was at it again, wasting that needlessly dignified voice of his on another idiotic broadcast...

lines.japanese: 「というわけで火曜日のレイディオＫＫ、次のコーナーはリスナー参加型のインタラクティブ・コンテンツ。皆さんの素敵なアイディアで、僕のモスト・デンジャラス・パーティーを成功に導いてください」
lines.english: “And so, on this Tuesday edition of Radio KK, our next segment is an interactive listener feature. Let your wonderful ideas help make my Most Dangerous Party a success.”

lines.japanese: 「全４８メニューのうち、ラスト・オンエアで決定したのはプログラムナンバー１１～１５の５種目。今回はその続きを埋めるべく、柳木原中からたくさんのメールをいただきました」
lines.english: “Of our forty-eight events, the last broadcast settled Programs Eleven through Fifteen. Today, to fill in what comes next, we have received a great many emails from across Yanagihara.”

lines.japanese: 「それでは行ってみましょう。一通目、プログラムナンバー１６に採用されたのは、美容院サロン・ド・シオマネキの従業員、痒いトコありま専科さんからいただいたこのメニュー。行ってみようレッツ、パーリィ」
lines.english: “Let us begin. Our first submission, selected as Program Number Sixteen, comes from No Itch Left Unscratched of the Salon de Fiddler Crab. Here we go—let's party!”

lines.japanese: 「題して『膣に陰茎を挿入するゲーム』！」
lines.english: “Its title: ‘The Game Where You Insert the Penis into the Vagina’!”

lines.japanese: 「続きはＣＭのあとで」
lines.english: “More after these messages.”

lines.japanese: ブツッ！
lines.english: Click!

lines.japanese: <8>\　どたどたどたたたたたた……！
lines.english: <8> Thud-thud-thud-thud-thud...!

lines.japanese: 「たっ、玉泉君！　ちょっと手を貸してくれ、この店内放送の成否は君の手にかかっている！　間もなく一回戦目が始まるぞ、時間がない、さあ早く来るんだ！」
lines.english: “M-Miss Tamaizumi! I need your help! The fate of this broadcast is in your hands! Round one is about to begin—there's no time! Come at once!”

lines.japanese: 「嫌です」
lines.english: “No.”
<10> “Wh-whaaat!?”

lines.japanese: いつも元気だなあマスターは。
lines.english: The boss never ran out of energy.

lines.japanese: 俺も眠くて仕事できるか不安だったけど、おかげで一気に目が覚めましたよ。
lines.english: I'd been worried I was too tired to work, but thanks to him I was wide awake now.

lines.japanese: 「おお鷲介、聞いてくれ。俺の大事な番組を、玉泉君がちっぽけなプライドを振りかざして邪魔するんだ」
lines.english: “Ah, Shusuke, listen to this. Miss Tamaizumi is brandishing her petty pride and sabotaging my precious program.”

lines.japanese: 「ふん、知りませんよ。マスターだって、せっかく俺がフリッキー５の曲を流そうと仕込んだのに、ちっぽけなエゴを振りかざして邪魔してくれたじゃないですか」
lines.english: “Hmph. Don't come crying to me. I went to all the trouble of slipping a Fricky Five song into the playlist, and you brandished your petty ego and sabotaged that.”

lines.japanese: 「ちぇっ、二人ともひどいよ」
lines.english: “Hmph. You're both horrible.”

lines.japanese: 「はいはい、仕事しましょーねー」
lines.english: “Yes, yes. Back to work.”

lines.japanese: 俺はしょぼくれた狩男と共に階段を上がっていきました。
lines.english: I headed upstairs with a dejected Karuo in tow.

lines.japanese: 「いらっしゃいませ！　お二人さまでよろしいですか？」
lines.english: “Welcome! Table for two?”

lines.japanese: 「喫煙席と禁煙席のどちらにご案内いたしましょう！」
lines.english: “Smoking or nonsmoking?”

lines.japanese: よーしよし、いい感じに頭が冴えてきた。
lines.english: Good, good. My head was clearing nicely.

lines.japanese: 見てください、フロアを縦横無尽に翔けるこの仕事っぷり！　これには鬼トレーナーの日和子さんとて、お褒めの言葉をかけたくなるってもんでしょう。
lines.english: Just look at me fly across every inch of this floor! Even Hiyoko, my merciless taskmaster, would have to praise work like this.

lines.japanese: 「千歳さん」
lines.english: “Mr. Chitose.”

lines.japanese: 「はいィッ！」
lines.english: “Ye-es!”

lines.japanese: 驚いた。まさか本当に向こうから声をかけてくるとは。
lines.english: Well, that was a surprise. I hadn't imagined she would actually speak to me first.

lines.japanese: しかしこれはチャンス。ここで仕事をもりもりこなして、日和子さんの好感度だってもりもりもり上げちゃうぞっ。
lines.english: But this was my chance. I'd tear through the work and send Hiyoko's affection meter shooting up, up, up!

lines.japanese: 「はいはい期待の中型新人、千歳鷲介です。ご用があればなんなりと」
lines.english: “Yes, yes—Shusuke Chitose, your much-touted middleweight rookie, at your service. Just say the word.”

lines.japanese: あれ？
lines.english: Huh?

lines.japanese: 日和子さんが俺を呼ぶからには、なにかしらの業務を仰せつかると思ってたんですけど……。
lines.english: If Hiyoko called me over, I naturally assumed she had some job for me...

lines.japanese: 「あの、なにか？」
lines.english: “Um, did you need something?”

lines.japanese: 日和子さんが無言なのでこっちから訊ねたら、下唇を噛むような表情。
lines.english: When her silence forced me to ask, she looked as though she were biting her lower lip.

lines.japanese: へ？　なんで？　俺、責められてる？　もしかしてなにか大事な仕事を忘れてる？
lines.english: Huh? Why? Was I in trouble? Had I forgotten some important job?

lines.japanese: 耳を澄ませば「昨日の……」とかなんとか、もごもごと口ごもっておられる御様子。え、昨日やりかけた仕事なんてあったっけ俺……？　や、やばい、覚えてないんですけど！
lines.english: When I strained my ears, I could just make out her mumbling something about “yesterday...” Had I left some job half-finished yesterday? Th-this was bad. I couldn't remember a thing!

lines.japanese: 「千歳さん」
lines.english: “Mr. Chitose.”

lines.japanese: 「は、はい」
lines.english: “Y-yes?”

lines.japanese: 「業務中は私語を慎むようにしてください」
lines.english: “Keep personal chatter to a minimum while we're on the clock.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ？　う、うそ、俺いま私語してた？　てか喋ってた？」
lines.english: “What? W-wait, was I having a personal conversation just now? Was I even talking?”

lines.japanese: 誰と？
lines.english: To whom?

lines.japanese: 周囲を見渡してみても、目が合う方はお皿の中のオマール海老さんしかいらっしゃいません。
lines.english: I looked around, but the only creature whose eye I caught was the lobster on a customer's plate.

lines.japanese: 「──ですが、止むを得ない場合にはその限りではありません」
lines.english: “—unless circumstances make such a conversation unavoidable.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、止むを得ず業務中に私語をするってどんな状況っすか」
lines.english: “What circumstances could possibly make chatting on the job unavoidable?”

lines.japanese: 「いまはお客様も少ないですし」
lines.english: “There aren't many customers at the moment.”

lines.japanese: 「そ、そうですねえ。まあ、少ないですねえ」
lines.english: “R-right. No, there aren't many at all.”

lines.japanese: 「フロアスタッフも充分に足りています」
lines.english: “And we have more than enough people on the floor.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ」
lines.english: “Uh-huh.”

lines.japanese: なんだこれ？　日和子さんが何かもの言いたげなのは分かるんだけど……。
lines.english: What was this? I could tell Hiyoko had something she wanted to say, but...

lines.japanese: あ！　もしかして、ちょっと早いけど、空いているいまのうちに休憩を取ってほしいってことか？
lines.english: Oh! Maybe it was a little early, but she wanted me to take my break now while things were quiet?

lines.japanese: トレーナーの都合みたいに思われるのが嫌で言いだしにくかったのかな。ははは、日和子さんもかわいらしいところがあるじゃないですか。
lines.english: Maybe she found it hard to say because she didn't want it to look as though she were arranging things for her own convenience. Ha ha! Hiyoko had an adorable side after all.

lines.japanese: ようがす。ここは誇り高き教官のため、自ら切りだしましょう。自己申告いたしましょう。
lines.english: Very well. For my proud coach's sake, I would bring it up myself. I would volunteer.

lines.japanese: 「そうだーあのー、ちょっと手も空いてるんで、自分いまのうち休憩入っちゃっていいすか？」
lines.english: “Oh, right—things are pretty quiet, so mind if I take my break now?”

lines.japanese: 「駄目です」
lines.english: “No.”

lines.japanese: 「ええっ」
lines.english: “What?!”

lines.japanese: な、なに言ってんだこの人。後輩とはいえ年長者が休憩に入りたいと言ってるわけですよ。しかも状況を踏まえた上で効率的に。それをアナタ一刀両断に駄目て。じゃあアナタ一体なにが言いたいのよ！
lines.english: Wh-what was wrong with this woman? I might be the new hire, but I was older than she was, and I had asked for my break with due regard for efficiency. Yet she cut me down with a single no. Then what in the world were you trying to say!?

lines.japanese: くうっ！　これって職権濫用ですよね？　後輩いびりですよね？　パワハラですよね？　いくらトレーナーだからって好き勝手やりやがって！
lines.english: Ghh! This was abuse of authority, wasn't it? Hazing the new guy! Workplace harassment! Just because she was my coach didn't mean she could do whatever she pleased!

lines.japanese: しかしこのまま振りまわされるわけにはいきません。ここは年上の男としてびっと言ってやりましょう。
lines.english: But I couldn't let her jerk me around forever. As the older man here, it was time I gave her a firm piece of my mind.

lines.japanese: 「おい貴様、いかに担当教官とはいえ、言っていいことと悪いことが――」
lines.english: “Now listen, you. I don't care if you're in charge of my training—there are things a person may say and things she—”
“Excuse me?”

lines.japanese: 「──あるわきゃないっすよね、も、ご用命とあらば何なりとお申しつけください！」
lines.english: “—may say without the slightest restriction! Whatever you command, you need only name it!”

lines.japanese: しかし教官様には逆らえない、純日本体質のわたくしでありました。滅私奉公、尽忠報国、進め鷲介火の玉だ！
lines.english: But I was Japanese to the core: I simply couldn't defy my instructor. Selfless service! Unswerving loyalty to the nation! Forward, Shusuke—a human fireball!

lines.japanese: 「あの、いまなら私もすこし手が空いてまして」
lines.english: “Um, I have a little time to spare myself just now.”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: あ、ああ、もしかしてそういうこと？
lines.english: Ah. Ahh. Was that what this was about?

lines.japanese: 分かった、分かりました、つまり日和子さんも息の抜き方を覚えたということですね？
lines.english: I got it. At last, I got it. Hiyoko had finally learned how to loosen up, hadn't she?

lines.japanese: それでこの俺と、お客さんのいない間に歓談でもいたしましょうと。ようがす、この千歳鷲介、伊達にひとの間をぬるぬると滑るように生きておりません。お任せください。
lines.english: And she wanted to enjoy a little chat with me while there were no customers around. Very well. Shusuke Chitose hadn't spent his life slipping smoothly between people for nothing. Leave it to me.

lines.japanese: 実は俺もさっきから、誰かに『いつだってプリズム』の感想を言いたくて仕方なかったんです。まあ彼女、自分の作品の話なんてされるの嫌がりそうだけど、ここはちょっとぐらい我慢してもらいましょうかね。
lines.english: The truth was, I'd been dying to tell somebody what I thought of *Always a Prism*. She probably hated talking about her own work, but she could put up with a little of it for once.

lines.japanese: 「いや、そうですよ。息抜きは大事ですよ。人間いつでも気を張ってたら疲れちゃいますもんね」
lines.english: “No, you're absolutely right. Taking a breather matters. Anyone would wear themselves out staying wound tight every minute of the day.”

lines.japanese: 「はい？」
lines.english: “Excuse me?”

lines.japanese: 「いやあ、普段からしっかりしてるもんで、日和子さんには疲れというものがないのかと思ってました」
lines.english: “You're always so put-together, I'd started to think you simply didn't get tired.”

lines.japanese: 「いえ、人並みには」
lines.english: “No. About as much as a regular person.”

lines.japanese: 「なに、人並みだと」
lines.english: “What? Regular?”

lines.japanese: 「あのうマスター、並なんて言葉にそこまで過剰反応するのは、マスターと牛丼屋の店員くらいですよ」
lines.english: “Um, Boss, the only people who should react that strongly to ‘regular’ are you and the staff behind a beef-bowl counter.”

lines.japanese: 「安心しろ玉泉君。君のサイズは世間の基準からしても恥じるべきところのない、むしろ誇るべきものだ。さあ、その牛並みの胸を張って張って張りまくるがいい」
lines.english: “Fear not, Miss Tamaizumi. Even by society's standards, your size is nothing to be ashamed of—indeed, it is a source of pride. So thrust out that magnificent bovine bosom! Thrust, and thrust, and thrust!”

lines.japanese: 「結構です」
lines.english: “No, thank you.”

lines.japanese: 「む。そうか、玉泉君は突きだすまでもなく、常時たゆんたゆんだったな。これは失礼した」
lines.english: “Hm. Of course. You are in a perpetual state of magnificent swaying without thrusting anything at all. My apologies.”

lines.japanese: 「謝るところを誤ってますね」
lines.english: “You're apologizing for the wrong thing.”

lines.japanese: 「黙っていろ鷲介。お前では性的興奮をもよおさん、俺を罵る役は玉泉君に任せておけ」
lines.english: “Silence, Shusuke. You do nothing for me sexually. Leave the insults to Miss Tamaizumi.”

lines.japanese: 「嫌です」
lines.english: “No.”

lines.japanese: 「なんだと、玉泉君は意外と器が小さいな」
lines.english: “What? Miss Tamaizumi, you're surprisingly small-minded.”

lines.japanese: 「器が小さいのはアナタですよ。マスター、俺がリクエストしたフリッキー５をぜんぜん流してくれないじゃないですか」
lines.english: “You're the small-minded one. Boss, you still haven't played any of the Fricky Five songs I requested.”

lines.japanese: 「ふん。前にも言ったろう、我がアレキサンダーではそんな軟弱な曲など流さんぞ」
lines.english: “Hmph. I told you before: Alexander will play no such spineless music.”

lines.japanese: どさくさに紛れて自分の要求を通そうかと思いましたが、マスターはそう易々とは折れてくれませんでした。ところが──
lines.english: I had tried to slip my own demand through amid the confusion, but the boss wasn't about to fold so easily. And then—

lines.japanese: 「そ、そういう曲も、たまにならいいと思いますが」
lines.english: “I-I think that sort of music might be all right once in a while.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: ──思わぬところから援護射撃が飛んできました。つうか、店内放送自体に反対してたはずの日和子さんが？　マジで？　うぞっ、どんな風の吹きまわし！？
lines.english: —covering fire came from an unexpected quarter. Hiyoko had opposed the in-house broadcast itself, hadn't she? Seriously? No way. What had gotten into her!?

lines.japanese: 「ちょっ、マスター聞きましたか！　あの岩石みたいに固いことでお馴染みの日和子さんですら賛同してくれましたよ！　これはもうフリファ流すしかないでしょう！」
lines.english: “Boss, did you hear that? Even Hiyoko, famous for being hard as a rock, agrees with me! You've got no choice but to play the Frickies now!”

lines.japanese: 「さりげなく失礼なことを言わないでください」
lines.english: “Please don't insult me so casually.”

lines.japanese: 「まったくだ、こんなに柔らかそうにたゆんでいるというのに」
lines.english: “Quite right. Not when she looks so soft and jiggly.”

lines.japanese: 「あからさまに失礼なことも言わないでください」
lines.english: “Please don't insult me blatantly either.”

lines.japanese: 「アルバム曲ですけど、フリファにも『煙突直行ベッドイン』っていうクリスマスソングもありますから！　ね、流しましょうよ！」
lines.english: “It's only an album track, but the Frickies have a Christmas song called ‘Straight Down the Chimney, Straight into Bed’! Come on, play it!”

lines.japanese: 「馬鹿をいえ。家族連れも訪れるこの店で、そんなストレートなタイトルのラブソングを流せるものか」
lines.english: “Don't be absurd. Families come to this restaurant. We cannot play a love song with a title that explicit.”

lines.japanese: 「自分のことだけ棚にあげ！？」
lines.english: “You're one to talk!”

lines.japanese: 「あの、ファミリー向けのクリスマスソングなら『ＹＯＵ　ＢＹ　三太クロス』がいいと思います」
lines.english: “Um, if you want a Christmas song for the whole family, I think ‘YOU BY Santa Cross’ would work.”
“...What?”

lines.japanese: 「ええ？　そんなマイナーな曲をよくご存知ですね。あれは子供番組とのタイアップ曲だけど、事務所的に黒歴史化されちゃっててあまり後世には残ってないんですよ」
lines.english: “What? You know a song that obscure? It was tied in with a children's program, but the agency buried it as an embarrassment, so almost no trace of it survived.”

lines.japanese: 「い、いえ、たまたま知っていただけですから」
lines.english: “I-I only happen to know it, that's all.”

lines.japanese: 「そんなことより、ほらほらマスター聞きました？　この通り、優秀な従業員二名からのリクエストが上がってるわけですよ！」
lines.english: “More to the point—Boss, you heard her! Two model employees have now submitted the same request!”

lines.japanese: 「むう、確かに玉泉君から賛成の声が上がるとは思っていなかったな」
lines.english: “Hm. I admit, I did not expect Miss Tamaizumi to support you.”

lines.japanese: 「べ、べつに……この店のＢＧＭには合ってると思っただけです……」
lines.english: “I-it isn't that... I only thought the music might suit this restaurant...”

lines.japanese: 「素晴らしい！　フリファの良さが分かるなんて、日和子さんは正しいものを見る目がおありっす！」
lines.english: “Wonderful! Hiyoko, you clearly have an unerring eye for quality—you appreciate the Frickies!”
“I see...”

lines.japanese: 「いや本当フリファはいいですよ？　いま聴いても通じる曲がありますよ？　というよりも、今だからこそ光る曲があるんです。フリファは老いてなお永遠の王子様ですからね」
lines.english: “No, really, the Frickies are great. Some of their songs still hold up today. More than that, some of them have only grown brighter with time. The men may grow old, but the Frickies will always be our princes.”

lines.japanese: 「まあ、そうですね」
lines.english: “Well, yes.”

lines.japanese: 俺がフリファについて力説していると、日和子さんが咳払いのような合いの手を入れてきました。
lines.english: As I held forth on the Frickies, Hiyoko punctuated my speech with a little throat-clearing sound.

lines.japanese: 「あの、千歳さんはだれが一番──」
lines.english: “Um, Mr. Chitose, which one is your favorite—”

lines.japanese: 「むっ、そういえば……おい鷲介、♪オーエス・オーエス・おまえの気持ちをエス・オー・エス～とかいう曲を知っているか」
lines.english: “Hm! Speaking of which... Shusuke, do you know the one that goes, ‘♪ Heave-ho, heave-ho, send your feelings S-O-S’?”

lines.japanese: 「え？　なんでマスター『左うちわで右肩上がり』なんて、フリッキー５後期の曲を知ってるんすか？」
lines.english: “What? Boss, how do you know ‘Easy Living, Rising Fortunes,’ from the Fricky Five's late period?”

lines.japanese: 「俺ではない。昨年行われた玉泉君の壮行会のカラオケで、彼女が披露してくれた歌を覚えていただけだ」
lines.english: “I don't, really. I only remember it because Miss Tamaizumi sang it at the karaoke party held in her honor last year.”

lines.japanese: 「へっ？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: マスターの視線を追うと、下唇を噛みながら目を逸らす日和子さんの姿がありました。
lines.english: I followed the boss's gaze and found Hiyoko looking away, biting her lower lip.

lines.japanese: 「え？　あの、もしかして日和子さん……好き、なんすかフリファ？」
lines.english: “Wait. Hiyoko... do you like the Frickies?”

lines.japanese: 「え、ええまあ……人並みには……」
lines.english: “W-well... about as much as the average person...”

lines.japanese: 「ははは、だから遠慮しなくていいと言っただろう。そのたゆんたゆんを人並みと言われては、人並み以上のものを持っている日野君ですら立場というものがあるまいて」
lines.english: “Ha ha ha! I told you there was no need for modesty. If you call that magnificent swaying average, even Miss Hino—who possesses rather more than the average woman—will find herself in a difficult position.”

lines.japanese: 「立場っつうか、さっきからあんたらの会話、全部聞こえてんすけどー」
lines.english: “Forget my position. I can hear every word you guys have been saying, you know.”

lines.japanese: 「あのー、どうしてこの店のスタッフは皆さん、会話に入るタイミングを窺いながら仕事してるんでしょうか」
lines.english: “Why does everyone here work with one ear on the conversation, waiting for the perfect moment to jump in?”

lines.japanese: 「違げーよ。邪魔かと思って遠慮してたんだよ、千歳がずっとたまひよの顔見てニヤけてるから」
lines.english: “That's not what I was doing. I held back because I thought I'd be interrupting. You've been staring at Tama-chick with a disgusting grin this whole time.”

lines.japanese: 「そ、そんな顔してませんよ失礼な！　ね、してませんよね日和子さん！」
lines.english: “I-I have not! How rude! Hiyoko, I haven't been making a face like that, have I?”

lines.japanese: 「すみません。千歳さんと話すときは顔を見ないので」
lines.english: “Sorry. I don't look at your face when I talk to you.”

lines.japanese: 「ノールックパス！？」
lines.english: “A no-look pass!?”

lines.japanese: 「フッ、このところ鷲介ばかりちやほやされて調子に乗っていたからな。ざまを見やがれ、これからは俺の時代だ」
lines.english: “Hmph. Shusuke has grown insufferably smug from all the attention he's been getting lately. Serves him right. From now on, it's my time.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ゴメン。店長は最初から審議対象外」
lines.english: “Oh, sorry. Manager, you were never in the running.”

lines.japanese: 「なんだと日野君、そんなことを言ってる暇があったら、さっさと仕事に戻りなさい」
lines.english: “What did you say, Miss Hino? If you have time for that nonsense, return to work at once.”

lines.japanese: 「店長もね」
lines.english: “That means you too, Manager.”

lines.japanese: ふたりは冷たい微笑みを交わしあいつつ、仕事に戻っていきました。
lines.english: The two exchanged icy smiles and went back to work.

lines.japanese: 「ところでたまひよってさ、去年の二次会で他にも三曲くらい歌ってたよね、フリなんとかの曲」
lines.english: “By the way, Tama-chick, didn't you sing three or so other songs by those Fricky-whatevers at last year's after-party?”

lines.japanese: 「えっ？　そうなんすか？」
lines.english: “What? Did she?”

lines.japanese: 「くふふ」
lines.english: “Heh heh.”

lines.japanese: 怪しい笑いを残して、今度こそ英里子さんは姿を消しました。
lines.english: Leaving that suspicious laugh behind, Eriko finally disappeared.

lines.japanese: あとに残された我々にはしばしの沈黙。
lines.english: The rest of us fell silent for a moment.

lines.japanese: 「あの、日和子さん……フリファ好きだったんすか……」
lines.english: “Um, Hiyoko... you really liked the Frickies...?”

lines.japanese: 「え、ええ、まあ……人並み、より多少は……」
lines.english: “W-well, yes... somewhat more than the average person...”

lines.japanese: 「や、お言葉ですが、カラオケで４曲も歌っちゃうのは多少じゃないですよね。マスターの言葉を借りたくないけど借りるなら、めちゃめちゃたゆんたゆんですよね」
lines.english: “Begging your pardon, but four songs at karaoke goes rather beyond ‘somewhat.’ I hate to borrow the boss's phrase, but if I must, you're jiggling like crazy.”

lines.japanese: 「くっ」
lines.english: “Ghk.”

lines.japanese: 「ですよね？」
lines.english: “Isn't it?”

lines.japanese: 「ええ、たゆんたゆんですが、それがなにか」
lines.english: “Yes, I'm jiggling like crazy. What of it?”

lines.japanese: うわ、逆ギレだあ。自分で振っといてなんだけど、開きなおると狩男ワードでも口にするんだなあ。
lines.english: Whoa, now she was getting mad at me. Granted, I'd set her up for that one, but once she decided to brazen it out, even Karuo's vocabulary was fair game.

lines.japanese: 「や、でも嬉しいっす！　こんな身近にフリファーの同志がいたなんて。ははは、日和子さん、もしかして昔はミーハーだったんすか？」
lines.english: “No, I'm thrilled! I can't believe a fellow Fricky fan was this close all along. Ha ha! Hiyoko, were you a real fangirl back in the day?”

lines.japanese: 「ミーハーというほどにはハマってません」
lines.english: “I was never into them enough to call myself a fangirl.”

lines.japanese: 「と思います」
lines.english: “...I think.”

lines.japanese: 「照れない照れない。仲間同士で隠すことないじゃないですか。俺なんか、いつでもひとに勧められるよう、復刻版のベストアルバムとかしょっちゅうバッグに入れっぱなしですよ」
lines.english: “No need to be shy. We're fellow fans—nothing to hide. I keep the reissued greatest-hits album in my bag all the time, just so I'm ready to recommend it to people.”

lines.japanese: 「復刻版……もしかして先月出た『ロシアン妊娠検査薬』ですか？」
lines.english: “The reissue... Do you mean *Russian Pregnancy Test*, the one that came out last month?”

lines.japanese: 「そっす、そっす。しかも限定生産の初回豪華版っすよ」
lines.english: “That's the one. And I've got the deluxe limited first edition.”

lines.japanese: 「うそ、見たい！」
lines.english: “No way! I want to see it!”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、ロッカーにありますよ。あとで見ます？」
lines.english: “It's in my locker. Want to look at it later?”

lines.japanese: 「見たい見たい！　私、初回版買いのがしちゃったの。ええそれって通常版とジャケット違うんでしょ──」
lines.english: “I do, I do! I missed the first edition. It has a different cover from the regular one, doesn't it—”

lines.japanese: 「──違うんですよね？　どんな感じでした？」
lines.english: “—it does, right? What was it like?”

lines.japanese: 「ええとホラ、通常版だとメンバー全員で路面電車に轢かれてるじゃないすか。アレがトロリーバスに変わってるんですよ。またそのヨッくんの表情が素晴らしくて──」
lines.english: “Well, you know how the regular edition shows all the members getting run over by a streetcar? The first edition swaps it for a trolleybus. And the expression on Yoshi's face is magnificent—”

lines.japanese: 「ヨッくんいい、細川君は！？」
lines.english: “Never mind Yoshi! What about Hosokawa?”

lines.japanese: 「あれ、食いつきいいすね。もしかして本命はホソリューすか？」
lines.english: “Wow, you really jumped on that. Is Hosoryu your favorite?”

lines.japanese: 「だって一番かっこいいじゃないですか！」
lines.english: “Of course! He's the best-looking one!”

lines.japanese: うわあ。
lines.english: Whoa.

lines.japanese: 日和子さんが両手を握りしめて身を乗りだしてきたので、俺は開いた両手を盾にして抑えこみました。
lines.english: Hiyoko clasped her hands and leaned eagerly toward me, so I raised both open palms as a shield and held her back.

lines.japanese: 「細川君いまだって『拘留されても愛してる』のドラマに出てるし、あ、あの原作って祥玄社さんから出てるんですよね」
lines.english: “Even now, Hosokawa's in the TV drama *I'll Love You Even in Detention*. Oh, a-and the original novel was published by Shogensha, wasn't it?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、でもヨッくんだって深夜の通販番組とか──」
lines.english: “Sure, but Yoshi does late-night shopping shows and—”

lines.japanese: 「ヨッくんいいです、それより細川君が来年、サスペンスもののドラマで主役やるの知ってます？」
lines.english: “Never mind Yoshi. Did you know Hosokawa's starring in a suspense drama next year?”

lines.japanese: 「ちょ、ちょっと待ってくださいよ！　何さらりと流してんすか、ヨッくんだっていいんすよ！　一番人気だけじゃダメなんすよ！　引き立て役がいてこそ、エースも光るってもんじゃないすか！」
lines.english: “W-wait a minute! You can't just brush him aside! Yoshi's great too! The most popular member can't do it all alone! The ace only shines because the supporting cast sets him off!”

lines.japanese: 人間出しゃばるとロクなことないすからねえ。というのはヨッくんこと足利美樹さんの残した至言です。
lines.english: Nothing good comes of pushing yourself into the spotlight, you know. Immortal words left to us by Miki Ashikaga, better known as Yoshi.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ千歳さんはヨッくんかマサシでも応援してればいいじゃないですか。私は細川君が好きなんです」
lines.english: “Then you can cheer for Yoshi or Masashi, Mr. Chitose. I like Hosokawa.”

lines.japanese: 「やっぱ日和子さんミーハーじゃん！」
lines.english: “So you are a fangirl after all!”

lines.japanese: 俺のツッコミで我に返ったのか、咳払いするようにこぶしで口元を押さえる日和子さん。
lines.english: That snapped Hiyoko back to herself. She covered her mouth with one fist as if clearing her throat.

lines.japanese: 「い、いいじゃないですか……千歳さんこそ、男性なのにフリッキー５が好きなんて珍しいですね」
lines.english: “A-and what's wrong with that...? You're the unusual one, Mr. Chitose—a man who likes the Fricky Five.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、まあ、そーなんすけどね」
lines.english: “Well, yeah, I suppose I am.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、恥ずかしがることはないですよ。ネットでも稀にいますし」
lines.english: “Oh, there's no need to be embarrassed. You do occasionally see male fans online.”

lines.japanese: 「たはは」
lines.english: “Ha ha.”

lines.japanese: あの日和子さんが俺のフォローをしてくれたので、こんなくだらないことだっていうのに照れてしまいました。
lines.english: Hiyoko, of all people, had tried to make me feel better. Ridiculous as the subject was, I found myself blushing.

lines.japanese: 「千歳さんはいつ頃から好きだったんですか？」
lines.english: “When did you start liking them, Mr. Chitose?”

lines.japanese: 「フリファが現役バリバリの頃からっすよ。いやあ、子供のころは憧れましたねえ。わずかな隙間から覗く彼らの、まあ羨ましいこと」
lines.english: “Back when the Frickies were still in their prime. Oh, how I admired them as a kid. What little I glimpsed of them through the gaps—God, how I envied those guys.”

lines.japanese: 「隙間？」
lines.english: “Gaps?”

lines.japanese: 「あっ！　いやいやいや！　こう、ね。うちの兄弟、チャンネル争いがすごいんすよ。テレビの前の陣取り合戦とか」
lines.english: “Ah! No, no, no! You see, my brothers and I fought fiercely over the channels. Battles for territory in front of the TV and all that.”

lines.japanese: 王位継承権とか？　≪コックピット≫とか？
lines.english: A claim to the throne, maybe? The *Cockpit*?

lines.japanese: 「あの、もしよかったら、あとで復刻版ほんとに見せてもらっていいですか？」
lines.english: “Um, if you really don't mind, may I see the reissue later?”

lines.japanese: 「もちろん、もちろん。じゃあ、あとで、スタッフルームでお会いしたときにでも」
lines.english: “Of course, of course. I'll show it to you when we're both in the staff room later.”

lines.japanese: 「はい」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 日和子さんは口元に手を当て、にこやかに微笑んでおられました。うーん、この人もだんだん息の抜き方を覚えてきたのかしら。
lines.english: Hiyoko held a hand to her mouth and smiled radiantly. Hmm. Maybe she was gradually learning how to loosen up after all.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあそれまでお仕事がんばりましょっか」
lines.english: “Then let's keep at it until we're done.”

lines.japanese: 「ええ、そうですね。仕事が終わったら──」
lines.english: “Yes, let's. Once work is over—”

lines.japanese: 「──千歳さん！　いま仕事中じゃないですか、業務中の私語は謹んでください！」
lines.english: “—Mr. Chitose! We're on the clock. Save the personal chatter!”

lines.japanese: 叩かれたテーブルの上で、オマール海老さんもびっくりして飛びあがりました。
lines.english: The lobster on the table gave a startled jump when Hiyoko slapped the tabletop.

lines.japanese: 「だいたい千歳さんは普段から……」
lines.english: “Honestly, Mr. Chitose, you always...”

lines.japanese: 「す、すみません、ちょっとトイレに」
lines.english: “S-sorry. Restroom.”

lines.japanese: 日和子さんのお説教タイムが始まったので、俺は海老のように丸まりながら化粧室へ駆けこみました。
lines.english: Hiyoko's lecture had begun, so I curled up like a shrimp and scurried off to the restroom.

lines.japanese: いやあ、それにしても日和子さんがフリファーだったなんてびっくりだあ。
lines.english: Still, what a surprise to discover that Hiyoko was a Fricky fan.

lines.japanese: ん？
lines.english: Hm?

lines.japanese: そういやフリファ騒動ですっかり流れちゃったけど、たしか彼女、その前に何か言いたそうたったよな？　アレって何を言おうとしてたんだろう。
lines.english: Come to think of it, the whole fuss over the Frickies had swept the earlier moment away, but she'd definitely looked as if she wanted to say something before that. What had she been about to tell me?

lines.japanese: ま、いいか。用があるなら向こうから言ってくるでしょう。
lines.english: Well, never mind. If it mattered, she'd tell me herself.
